predecessors.name: West Francia
predecessors.text: Anjou, 'roughly co-extensive with the diocese of Angers', a county of West Francia since the first count 'appointed: 861'

successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: Anjou and Maine, reunited with the crown when Philip of Valois was recognised as king on 1 April 1328

ledger.x: 990: the county of Anjou stands as a great fief of the Capetian kingdom under Fulk III.
1044: Nouy ends the war for Touraine.
1044: Tours, Chinon and Langeais pass to Anjou.
1051: Geoffrey takes Le Mans and Maine.
1062: Saintonge goes to the Duke of Aquitaine.

1126: Cliopatria continues the county's polygon (26,690 km2) as the Angevins row to 1146 and then as the Angevin Empire to 1209 (bridging; the County page has Geoffrey V Plantagenet 1129-1151, Normandy received on 19 January 1144, Henry II recognised as king on 19 December 1154, Philip II's conquest of Anjou in…
1290: Anjou and Maine pass to Charles of Valois.
1328: Anjou and Maine are reunited with the crown.
1328: the county of Anjou is absorbed into the royal domain; the later Duchy of Anjou (1360) is carried by the house-of-valois-anjou dossier.

wars.name: Battle of Nouy
wars.outcome: Angevin victory on 21 August 1044; Theobald III of Blois captured and Tours, Chinon and Langeais surrendered.

wars.name: Norman-Angevin struggle for Alençon and Domfront
wars.outcome: William besieged Alençon (1049-1051) and Domfront (winter of 1052); the Norman dossier has Passais taken in 1050.

wars.name: Battle of Mortemer
wars.outcome: 'In late January, early February 1054, Count Geoffrey and King Henry together invaded Normandy'; the invasion failed.

wars.name: Battle of Varaville
wars.outcome: 'Duke William launched a sudden attack and defeated them'; no border change.

wars.name: Norman conquest of Maine
wars.outcome: 'William invaded Maine in force in 1063' and 'controlled the county by the beginning of 1064'; the Angevin hold on Maine ends.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a treaty or surveyed frontier for Anjou; the county is described as 'roughly co-extensive with the diocese of Angers'.
